top.line: Agent sessions with one mandate can be paused for weeks and resumed with their record, so knowledge outlives the team.
top.para: When project teams dissolve, the knowledge to change their systems leaves with them. Agent sessions focused on one mandate, role and repository can be paused and picked up again with the conversation, reasoning and code intact. Sessions on the sgit CLI and SG/Send have resumed after 36 and 43 days, straight into tested work. A newcomer inherits the history and agents ready to act.

in-short.line: Teams dissolve and knowledge leaves; agent sessions can be paused and resumed, as the sgit teams show over weeks.
in-short.para: Projects end and knowledge leaves with people, which makes later fixes hard. Agent sessions with one mandate, role and repository can be paused and resumed with their record intact. Sessions on the sgit CLI and SG/Send resumed after 36 and 43 days; two PHP-team sessions after 28 hours. A newcomer inherits a team, not just code.

the-team-that-leaves.line: Every team peaks and then dissolves, and the knowledge goes with the people, until a fix is needed.
the-team-that-leaves.para: A project's sharp team moves on when it dries out, meets its goals or is sold. The know-how, architecture, undocumented reasons and insights leave too. When a fix is needed, as for old PHP now, nobody knows the side effects, and sometimes the pipeline to build and ship the code no longer works.

one-mandate.line: The newsroom and the PHP story run on sessions with one mandate each, which can be paused and resumed.
one-mandate.para: Each agent session does one piece of work with one mandate, role and repository; the PHP story had twenty by 23 October. They keep lessons and debriefs and release their own work. Such a session can be paused at no cost and resumed later with its conversation, reasoning and decisions intact.

sgit-teams.line: Sessions on the sgit CLI and SG/Send resumed after 36 and 43 days, from current code, straight into tested work.
sgit-teams.para: The sgit CLI and SG/Send teams have dedicated sessions whose commits name them. One SG/Send session paused 43 days, resumed from dev 19 releases later and shipped a container image with 36 green tests. A CLI session returned after 15 days with 3,822 tests passing. Each repo also has many short sessions, and a commit gap does not prove idleness.

this-week.line: On a short scale, two PHP-team sessions resumed after 28 hours by first taking in the team's work.
this-week.para: The librarian last committed at 20:20 UTC on 22 October and resumed at 00:12 on 24 October by merging dev before its pass. The cartographer resumed at 00:16 with 76 new parties resolved and was renamed the ontologist. Nothing depends on the gap's length: a day or a quarter.

why-powerful.line: A frozen team can be woken when a fix lands, and a newcomer inherits the history and agents ready to act.
why-powerful.para: Systems went dark this week because their builders had moved on. A frozen team could be woken, read the advisory, know the side effects from its own tests, and propose the change. A new developer inherits the history, materials and agents, and maintenance by the people who know the code becomes cheap enough to sell.

what-it-takes.line: It takes habits: one mandate per session, a written record, a living pipeline, catching up first, keys handed over.
what-it-takes.para: It works because each session has one mandate, writes lessons, debriefs and briefs into the repository, keeps the build and tests running, catches up before acting, and receives keys through a handshake rather than holding secrets indefinitely.

limits.line: The longest observed pause is 43 days; commits are the evidence; context has limits; people still decide.
limits.para: Years is the design's promise, not a measurement. A session that commits nothing may still have been open, and the repos also have many short sessions. Long sessions summarise their history, so the written record matters. The platform must keep the session and the repository must outlive it. Agents keep knowledge within reach; someone still decides.

sources.line: My memos, the CLI and SG/Send git histories by session, the PHP story's history and status page.
sources.para: My voice memos of 24 October 2026; the git histories of SGit-AI__CLI and SGraph-AI__App__Send, all branches, keyed on the session in each commit; the PHP story site's git history from 22 to 24 October and its team status page; and related articles on agents writing, almost working, maintenance and the PHP updates.
